posts.author: Theponidraws
posts.body:
Hi! So I'm making a game with my friend for a school project, and we made the sprites for the characters, but they look too small for the game. Plus, it kinda loses the quality when they are placed in the game. I also thought that maybe the problem is that the maps are too big? But my thoughts are that the sprites are actually too small. If anyone can give me advice on how to correct this, I would appreciate it very much! I upload an image of how they look in game and how they are. Oh, and I used Ibis paint to draw them!! (If that helps)

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Is that Amy walking sprite attachment the actual file that you're using in the game? Because that's freaking huge. It's also formatted a bit poorly - there's some extra space that you don't want on all sides of every cel.
(you also shouldn't have filenames with spaces in them in your project)
Did you also draw the tiles for your map? Or did you draw it externally and you're using parallax maps?
Are you using any plugins in the project? If yes, did you do the basic troubleshooting step of turning those plugins off?
Have you made practice games using the artwork that comes with MV? Do you understand how the map tiles work?
It's almost impossible to tell anything else just from those pictures except that the image you attached is humongous.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
Theponidraws said:
And I don't understand what do you mean with formatted poorly?
Click to expand...
there is no fixed size to the sprites, sprites can be any size.
what defines the sprite is the sprite structure: 3x4 cells with the sprites centered into each cell. And your sprites are not correctly centered.
perhaps the following tutorial will help your understanding of cells and sprite structures and how to make larger sprites:
How to create your own templates (any sprite or battler sheet)
Time and time again people who want to create their own sprites are asking for pre-made empty/framed templates because they can't work without them. And they don't even understand how limiting that is.  Templates are crutches - bad crutches to be precise, because if you need a premade template...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com

Not quite. Tiles (not tales) are 48x48 squares. You can draw characters to be larger or smaller than that, but when you take one step on the map, it will move 48 pixels.
And when you're placing events on top of your parallax map to block off where the character can't walk, those are in 48 pixel squares.
If you need any more help figuring it out, you need to attach some of the actual images you're using in your game.
